stem: A research computing team needs to run a queue of thousands of independent Monte Carlo simulation jobs to completion, then scale all compute back to zero until the next batch arrives.

choices.text: AWS Fargate running a single long-lived ECS service
AWS Lambda invoking each simulation directly

rationale: AWS Batch provisions the EC2, ECS Managed Instances, or Fargate capacity a queued job needs and scales that capacity down to zero once the queue empties, which is exactly this run-to-completion, scale-to-zero job pattern. Amazon EMR partitions one large dataset across a cluster's nodes for distributed Hadoop or Spark analytics; it is not built around a queue of many independent jobs. Fargate running a single long-lived ECS service is designed to keep a service continuously running, not to scale an entire fleet to zero between batches of queued jobs. Invoking each simulation directly from Lambda skips the job-queue and compute-environment management Batch provides, and Lambda's execution limits make it a poor fit for long-running simulation jobs at this scale.
